library(shiny)        #To load shiny web app
library(tidyverse)    #For data manipulation and graphs
library(readxl)       #To load the excel (.xlsx/.xls) files
library(patchwork)    #To patch multiple graphs generated into one.
library(lubridate)    #For date
# -----------------------------
# Helper functions
# -----------------------------

#Now creating a function that will normalize the header so that we can make the app more robust
#str_squish() removes any line change or multiple spaces into single space. It makes reading headers more consistent.

normalize_header <- function(x) {
  x |>
    str_squish() |>
    str_to_lower()
}
#Now, we create another function to detect the animal we have, feline or canine
#First we use the normalized or cleaned header ans then search for words feline or cat and dog or canine.

detect_species <- function(headers) {
  headers_clean <- normalize_header(headers)
  
  #here we use \b which is like the boundary, searching for the whole word.
  #this avoids mistaking words like catenibacterium, catalog, indicate, etc which has "cat" inside it.
  #str_detect checks the cleaned header for strings or character we specify.
  
  has_feline <- any(str_detect(headers_clean, "\\bfeline\\b|\\bcat\\b"))
  has_canine <- any(str_detect(headers_clean, "\\bcanine\\b|\\bdog\\b"))
  
  #we check and return the species it has
  
  if (has_feline && !has_canine) return("cat")
  if (has_canine && !has_feline) return("dog")
  if (has_feline && has_canine) return("mixed_or_unclear")
  
  #if there is no cat or dog then it returns unknown
  
  "unknown"
}

#now we have another function which will help us find the columns even if the name is not exact
#it will look at the patterns that I gave below and match with the columns in the file uploaded by the user
#first we get the cleaned headers

find_col <- function(df, patterns) {
  headers <- normalize_header(names(df))
  #the above changed all of the column names from df into normalized forms and saved as headers
  match_index <- which(map_lgl(headers, function(h) {
    any(str_detect(h, patterns))
  }))
  #map_lgl is interesting one...it can be utilized with a function inside it.
  #this will detect the patterns (all the listed variations of each of the headers in the map below) and return true/false to map the index
  #here h is like one column header at a time, so it goes through every column name one by one
  #then, for each column name it gives true or false pattern
  #finally, this function will find the column names with matching pattern as listed below
  
  #if noting matched, return no characters and if matched, take the first matching position  
  if (length(match_index) == 0) return(NA_character_)
  
  names(df)[match_index[1]]
}

#it would take a data frame and a list of possible name pattern for one bacterium, find the actual column to match the pattern and give the real name as in the input file.


#now, we have another function which take raw input form our file and cleans the column names 

clean_names_robust <- function(df) {
  names(df) <- names(df) |>
    str_squish() |>
    str_to_lower()
  
  #then we run the species detector on cleaned column names, storing results in species.   
  species <- detect_species(names(df))
  
  #below is the pattern that we search for in the column headers
  #we can still work on this to make out app more robust
  
  col_map <- list(
    AnimalName = c("\\bcat name\\b","\\bcatname\\b", "\\bdogname\\b", "\\bdog name\\b", "\\banimal name\\b", "\\bpatient name\\b"),
    DI = c("feline dysbiosis index", "canine dysbiosis index", "dysbiosis index", "dog index", "cat index", "\\bdi\\b", "canine index", "feline index"),
    Faecali = c("faecalibacterium", "fecalibacterium"),
    Turici = c("turicibacter"),
    Strep = c("streptococcus"),
    Coli = c("e\\. coli", "escherichia coli"),
    Blautia = c("blautia"),
    Fuso = c("fusobacterium"),
    Hiranonis = c("hiranonis" , "peptacetobacter hiranonis", "clostridium hiranonis"),
    Bifido = c("bifidobacterium"),
    Bacteriodes = c("bacteriodes", "bacteroides"),
    Clostridium = c("clostridium perfringens"),
    Entero = c("enterococcus"),
    Lacto = c("lactobacillus"),
    Oscillo = c("oscillospiraceae", "ruminococcaceae"),
    Collin = c("collinsella", "collinesella"),
    Sega = c("segatella", "prevotella copri", "prevotella"),
    Mega = c("megamonas"),
    Medi = c("mediterraneibacter gnavus", "ruminococcus gnavus", "gnavus"),
    Date = c("^date$"),
    SampleID = c("\\bsample id\\b"),
    InternalID = c("internal id"),
    Group = c("^group$", "\\btreatment group\\b", "\\bexperimental group\\b", "\\bcondition\\b", "\\bcategory\\b"),
    TotalBActeria = c("total bacteria", "bacterial log dna"),
    Cdifficile = c("difficile"),
    Parvo = c("parvo"),
    netF = c("net F toxin"),
    Cjejuni = c("Campylobacter"),
    Tricho = c("Tritrichomonas")
  )
  #now, from the above patterns we have, we use find_col function to search for pattern and
  #for the matched columns, we store them in found_cols. found_cols will have the name from col_map and it has a character wich is the normalized heder which matched to patterns.
  #So it will have the new name we assigned to the patterns it matched in the input excel headers plus the normalized header.
  
  found_cols <- map_chr(col_map, ~ find_col(df, .x))
  
  #here .x means the entire list for each of the headers in the map.
  #so find_col uses it to search for match in the headers of the df we have, input excel file
  
  #now we extract the new names or the headers of the found_cols.
  #then we also extract the old_name which is the normalized original column names
  #then if there is old name, we just remove the old names and put the new names, or the simple names as in the col_map
  
  for (new_name in names(found_cols)) {
    old_name <- found_cols[[new_name]]
    
    if (!is.na(old_name)) {
      names(df)[names(df) == old_name] <- new_name
    }
  }
  
  #now we attach the species that we detected and attached to the dataframe without disturbing it. 
  attr(df, "species") <- species
  
  df
}
#the above function will now give the data frame with cleaner column names, for all the patterns we suspected it might be given as names.
#this clean_name_robust makes out app more robust and cleans the column names

convert_plot_columns <- function(df) {
  
  plot_columns <- c(
    "DI",
    "Faecali",
    "Turici",
    "Strep",
    "Coli",
    "Blautia",
    "Fuso",
    "Hiranonis",
    "Bifido",
    "Bacteriodes",
    "Clostridium",
    "Entero",
    "Lacto",
    "Oscillo",
    "Collin",
    "Sega",
    "Mega",
    "Medi"
  )
  
  columns_present <- intersect(plot_columns, names(df))
  
  df |>
    mutate(
      across(
        all_of(columns_present),
        ~ suppressWarnings(
          readr::parse_number(as.character(.x))
        )
      )
    )
}

# Convert numbers to letters:
# 1 = a, 2 = b, ..., 26 = z, 27 = aa
number_to_letters <- function(number) {
  
  result <- ""
  
  while (number > 0) {
    number <- number - 1
    
    result <- paste0(
      letters[(number %% 26) + 1],
      result
    )
    
    number <- number %/% 26
  }
  
  result
}


# Replace long x-axis labels with short letter codes
shorten_x_axis_labels <- function(plot_df, maximum_characters = 12) {
  
  original_labels <- unique(
    as.character(plot_df$XLabel)
  )
  
  original_labels <- original_labels[
    !is.na(original_labels) &
      original_labels != ""
  ]
  
  has_long_labels <- any(
    nchar(original_labels) > maximum_characters
  )
  
  # If no labels are long, leave everything unchanged
  if (!has_long_labels) {
    plot_df$XAxisKeyText <- NA_character_
    return(plot_df)
  }
  
  short_labels <- vapply(
    seq_along(original_labels),
    number_to_letters,
    character(1)
  )
  
  label_key <- tibble(
    OriginalLabel = original_labels,
    ShortLabel = short_labels
  )
  
  plot_df <- plot_df |>
    mutate(
      OriginalXLabel = as.character(XLabel),
      
      ShortXLabel = label_key$ShortLabel[
        match(OriginalXLabel, label_key$OriginalLabel)
      ],
      
      XLabel = factor(
        ShortXLabel,
        levels = short_labels
      ),
      
      XAxisKeyText = paste(
        paste0(
          label_key$ShortLabel,
          " = ",
          label_key$OriginalLabel
        ),
        collapse = "\n"
      )
    )
  
  plot_df
}

#now, we are preparing the animal data
#first, we look for date. If there is date in the file we have for looking into time point analysis or change of DI
#so this app will not run if there is no data or DI in the input file.

prep_animal_data <- function(df, x_axis) {
  
  validate(
    need(
      "DI" %in% names(df),
      "Could not find a Dysbiosis Index column."
    ),
    need(
      !is.null(x_axis) &&
        x_axis %in% names(df),
      "Please select a valid x-axis column."
    )
  )
  
  selected_values <- df[[x_axis]]
  
  # Determine whether the selected column represents dates
  is_date_column <- (
    str_detect(
      normalize_header(x_axis),
      "date"
    ) ||
      inherits(
        selected_values,
        c("Date", "POSIXct", "POSIXt")
      )
  )
  
  if (is_date_column) {
    
    if (is.numeric(selected_values)) {
      
      parsed_dates <- as.Date(
        selected_values,
        origin = "1899-12-30"
      )
      
    } else if (
      inherits(
        selected_values,
        c("Date", "POSIXct", "POSIXt")
      )
    ) {
      
      parsed_dates <- as.Date(selected_values)
      
    } else {
      
      parsed_dates <- suppressWarnings(
        as.Date(
          lubridate::parse_date_time(
            as.character(selected_values),
            orders = c(
              "mdy",
              "ymd",
              "dmy",
              "Ymd",
              "m/d/Y",
              "Y/m/d",
              "d-b-Y",
              "d-b-y"
            )
          )
        )
      )
    }
    
    df |>
      mutate(
        SelectedDate = parsed_dates
      ) |>
      filter(!is.na(SelectedDate)) |>
      arrange(SelectedDate) |>
      mutate(
        XValue = format(
          SelectedDate,
          "%m/%d/%Y"
        ),
        XLabel = factor(
          XValue,
          levels = unique(XValue)
        )
      )
    
  } else {
    
    df |>
      filter(
        !is.na(.data[[x_axis]]),
        as.character(.data[[x_axis]]) != ""
      ) |>
      mutate(
        XValue = as.character(
          .data[[x_axis]]
        ),
        XLabel = factor(
          XValue,
          levels = unique(XValue)
        )
      )
  }
}

#The above takes non-empty dates or removes dates which could not be converted and then arranges 
#arrange sorts the entire df according to the date in ascending order
#then mutate creates a new column IDLabel converts date into US style and then makes it into factor
#the level of this factor is not according to the date.
#another important thing is that we only take unique data. So, we take only one unique date (no multiple common date) and the readings from that date


#now, making a base theme for plots so that we do not have to repeat it
#enter inofrmation like the graph style, font size for titles, axis labels, etc.

base_plot_theme <- function() {
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "italic", size = 14, hjust = 0.5),
      axis.title.y = element_text(face = "plain", size = 8.5), 
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), #angle for the x-axis label (date)
      legend.position = "none" #removed the legend to save space
    )
}

add_scatter_points <- function(p, plot_df, variable) {
  
  # Keep rows that have an actual measurement for this panel
  valid_plot_df <- plot_df |>
    filter(!is.na(.data[[variable]]))
  
  # Keep only x-axis values containing two or more measurements
  median_df <- valid_plot_df |>
    add_count(XLabel, name = "PointCount") |>
    filter(PointCount > 1)
  
  # Plot every individual observation
  p <- p +
    geom_jitter(
      data = valid_plot_df,
      width = 0.15,
      height = 0,
      size = 1.2,
      color = "black",
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  
  # Add a red median only where an x-axis value has multiple points
  if (nrow(median_df) > 0) {
    p <- p +
      stat_summary(
        data = median_df,
        fun = median,
        geom = "point",
        shape = 95,
        size = 10,
        color = "red",
        na.rm = TRUE
      )
  }
  
  p
}

#To make bacterial plot
make_panel_plot <- function(
    plot_df,
    variable,
    title,
    legend_label,
    normal_low = NULL,
    normal_high = NULL,
    y_limits = c(0, 10),
    y_breaks = waiver()
) {
  
  p <- ggplot(
    plot_df,
    aes(x = XLabel, y = .data[[variable]])
  )
  
  # Add the gray reference interval
  if (!is.null(normal_low) && !is.null(normal_high)) {
    p <- p +
      annotate(
        "rect",
        xmin = -Inf,
        xmax = Inf,
        ymin = normal_low,
        ymax = normal_high,
        fill = "grey75",
        alpha = 0.6
      ) +
      geom_hline(
        yintercept = c(normal_low, normal_high),
        linetype = "dashed",
        color = "black",
        linewidth = 0.4
      )
  }
  if (variable == "Hiranonis") {
    p <- p +
      geom_hline(
        yintercept = 4,
        linetype = "dotdash",
        color = "red",
        linewidth = 0.8)
  }
  
  p <- add_scatter_points(
    p = p,
    plot_df = plot_df,
    variable = variable
  )
  
  p +
    scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(add = 0.6)) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      limits = y_limits,
      breaks = seq(
        from = y_limits[1],
        to = y_limits[2],
        by = 2
      ),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))
    ) +
    labs(
      title = title,
      x = NULL,
      y = "log DNA"
    ) +
    base_plot_theme()
}

#Now making DI plot

make_di_plot <- function(plot_df, species = "unknown") {
  
  y_label <- case_when(
    species == "cat" ~ "Feline dysbiosis index",
    species == "dog" ~ "Canine dysbiosis index",
    TRUE ~ "Dysbiosis index"
  )
  
  if (species == "dog") {
    max_di <- 2
    y_scale <- c(-10, 10)
    ticks <- seq(-10, 10, by = 2)
  } else {
    max_di <- 1
    y_scale <- c(-5, 5)
    ticks <- seq(-5, 5, by = 1)
  }
  
  p <- ggplot(
    plot_df,
    aes(x = XLabel, y = DI)
  ) +
    annotate(
      "rect",
      xmin = -Inf,
      xmax = Inf,
      ymin = -Inf,
      ymax = 0,
      fill = "grey65",
      alpha = 0.6
    ) +
    annotate(
      "rect",
      xmin = -Inf,
      xmax = Inf,
      ymin = 0,
      ymax = max_di,
      fill = "grey90",
      alpha = 0.6
    ) +
    geom_hline(
      yintercept = c(0, max_di),
      linetype = "dashed",
      color = "black",
      linewidth = 0.4
    )
  
  p <- add_scatter_points(
    p = p,
    plot_df = plot_df,
    variable = "DI"
  )
  
  p +
    scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(add = 0.6)) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      limits = y_scale,
      breaks = ticks
    ) +
    labs(
      title = "Dysbiosis Index",
      x = NULL,
      y = y_label
    ) +
    base_plot_theme() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(
        face = "plain",
        size = 14,
        hjust = 0.5
      )
    )
}

get_panel_info <- function(species) {
  if (species == "dog") {
    canine_panel
  } else {
    feline_panel
  }
}

make_available_plots <- function(plot_df, species) {
  panel_info <- get_panel_info(species)
  
  plots <- list(
    di = make_di_plot(plot_df, species)
  )
  
  available_panel <- panel_info |>
    filter(variable %in% names(plot_df))
  
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(available_panel))) {
    row <- available_panel[i, ]
    
    normal_low <- row$normal_low
    normal_high <- row$normal_high
    
    if (is.na(normal_low) || is.na(normal_high)) {
      normal_low <- NULL
      normal_high <- NULL
    }
    
    plots[[row$variable]] <- make_panel_plot(
      plot_df = plot_df,
      variable = row$variable,
      title = row$title,
      legend_label = row$legend_label,
      normal_low = normal_low,
      normal_high = normal_high,
      y_limits = c(row$y_min, row$y_max)
    )
  }
  
  plots
}

wrap_plot_page <- function(plot_list, ncol = 4) {
  if (length(plot_list) == 0) {
    return(
      ggplot() +
        theme_void() +
        labs(title = "No matching bacterial columns found.")
    )
  }
  
  wrap_plots(plot_list, ncol = ncol)
}

make_fixed_slots <- function(plots, slot_names) {
  
  map(
    slot_names,
    function(plot_name) {
      
      if (plot_name %in% names(plots)) {
        plots[[plot_name]]
      } else {
        plot_spacer()
      }
    }
  )
}



make_page1 <- function(plot_df, species) {

  if (species == "dog") {

      "Faecali",

      "Coli",
      "Strep",
      "Faecali",

      "Bifido",
      "Bacteriodes"
    )

}

    nrow = 3
  )
  
  page_body +
    plot_annotation(
      title = paste(
        str_to_title(species),
        "- Extended PCR"
      ),
      theme = theme(
        plot.title = element_text(
          face = "bold",
          size = 14,
          hjust = 0.5
        )
      )
    )
}

# Shiny app
# -----------------------------


ui <- fluidPage(
  tags$head(
    tags$style(HTML("
      .help-block {
        color: #000000 !important; /* Forces the color to solid black */
        font-weight: 500;          /* Optional: makes it slightly sharper */
      }
    "))
  ),
  
  titlePanel("Dysbiosis Panel"),
  
  sidebarLayout(
    
    sidebarPanel(
      width = 2,
      
      fileInput(
        "file",
        "Upload excel file",
        accept = c(".xlsx", ".xls")
      ),
      
      uiOutput("x_axis_selector"),
      uiOutput("species_text"),
      uiOutput("x_axis_key"),
      
      helpText("    Use this tool to visualize your Excel data for canine or feline dysbiosis. The first page displays Disbiosis index (DI) and its bacterial panel graphs. The second page displays the graphs for extended bacterial PCR. The third page allows you to preview your uploaded data."),
      
      tags$ul(
        tags$li("Upload your Excel sheet (.xlsx or .xls) to begin."),
        tags$li("Select the column or grouping variable for your comparison."),
        tags$li("View the results in scatter plot across individuals or groups."),
        tags$li("Grouped comparisons will highlight the median (red line) for each category.")
      ),
      helpText(
        "Note: The red dot-dash at the 4 logDNA in",
        tags$i("P. hiranonis"),
        "graph represents the threshold for predicted abnormal unconjugated bile acid (BA) conversion."
      ),
    ),
    
    mainPanel(
      width = 10,
      
      tabsetPanel(
        tabPanel(
          "DI Panel",
          uiOutput("page1_container")
        ),
        tabPanel(
          "Extended PCR",
          uiOutput("page2_container")
        ),
        tabPanel(
          "Data Preview",
          tableOutput("preview")
        )
      )
    )
  )
)
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  raw_data <- reactive({
    req(input$file)
    
    read_excel(input$file$datapath) |>
      clean_names_robust() |>
      convert_plot_columns()
  })
  
  species <- reactive({
    attr(raw_data(), "species")
  })
  
  output$species_text <- renderUI({
    req(raw_data())
    
    detected <- species()
    
    if (detected == "cat") {
      strong("Detected species: Cat / Feline")
    } else if (detected == "dog") {
      strong("Detected species: Dog / Canine")
    } else if (detected == "mixed_or_unclear") {
      strong("Detected species: unclear because both feline/cat and canine/dog were found in headers.")
    } else {
      strong("Detected species: unknown")
    }
  })
  output$x_axis_selector <- renderUI({
    df <- raw_data()
    
    measurement_cols <- c(
      "DI", "Faecali", "Turici", "Strep", "Coli",
      "Blautia", "Fuso", "Hiranonis", "Bifido",
      "Bacteriodes", "Clostridium", "Entero",
      "Lacto", "Oscillo", "Collin", "Sega", "Mega",
      "Medi", "TotalBActeria",
      "Cdifficile", "Parvo", "netF", "Cjejuni", "Tricho"
    )
    
    metadata_cols <- setdiff(names(df), measurement_cols)
    
    excluded_x_axis_patterns <- paste(
      c(
        "dysbiosis index",
        "log dna",
        "total bacteria",
        "c\\. difficile",
        "clostridioides difficile",
        "parvovirus",
        "\\bparvo\\b",
        "\\bnet\\s*f\\b",
        "toxin gene",
        "campylobacter",
        "tritrichomonas",
        "\\bresult\\b",
        "note"
      ),
      collapse = "|"
    )
    
    metadata_cols <- metadata_cols[
      !str_detect(
        normalize_header(metadata_cols),
        excluded_x_axis_patterns
      )
    ]
    
    metadata_cols <- metadata_cols[
      vapply(metadata_cols, function(column_name) {
        values <- df[[column_name]]
        
        any(
          !is.na(values) &
            trimws(as.character(values)) != ""
        )
      }, logical(1))
    ]
    
    validate(
      need(
        length(metadata_cols) > 0,
        "No non-empty metadata columns are available for the x-axis."
      )
    )
    
    selectInput(
      inputId = "x_axis",
      label = "Select the column for comparison.",
      choices = metadata_cols,
      selected = metadata_cols[1]
    )
  })
  
  plot_data <- reactive({
    
    req(input$x_axis)
    
    df <- prep_animal_data(
      df = raw_data(),
      x_axis = input$x_axis
    )
    
    validate(
      need(
        nrow(df) > 0,
        "No usable rows were found for this selection."
      )
    )
    
    # Replace labels longer than 12 characters
    df <- shorten_x_axis_labels(
      plot_df = df,
      maximum_characters = 12
    )
    
    df
  })
  
  output$x_axis_key <- renderUI({
    
    df <- plot_data()
    
    key_text <- df$XAxisKeyText[
      !is.na(df$XAxisKeyText)
    ]
    
    # Show nothing when labels were not shortened
    if (length(key_text) == 0) {
      return(NULL)
    }
    
    key_lines <- strsplit(
      key_text[1],
      split = "\n",
      fixed = TRUE
    )[[1]]
    
    tagList(
      tags$hr(),
      
      tags$strong("X-axis label key"),
      
      tags$div(
        style = paste0(
          "margin-top: 8px;",
          "max-height: 350px;",
          "overflow-y: auto;",
          "overflow-x: hidden;",
          "font-size: 12px;",
          "line-height: 1.4;",
          "word-break: break-word;",
          "background-color: white;",
          "border: 1px solid #dddddd;",
          "padding: 8px;"
        ),
        
        lapply(
          key_lines,
          function(key_line) {
            tags$div(
              style = "margin-bottom: 5px;",
              key_line
            )
          }
        )
      )
    )
  })
  
  output$page1_container <- renderUI({
    
    df <- plot_data()
    
    number_of_x_points <- n_distinct(
      df$XLabel,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
    
    # Each individual graph receives more horizontal space
    # when more x-axis values are present
    individual_panel_width <- max(
      320,
      140 + (number_of_x_points * 35)
    )
    
    # Page 1 has four graph columns
    complete_page_width <- individual_panel_width * 4
    
    tags$div(
      style = paste0(
        "width: 100%;",
        "overflow-x: auto;",
        "overflow-y: hidden;",
        "display: block;"
      ),
      
      plotOutput(
        outputId = "page1",
        
        # Dynamic width
        width = paste0(
          complete_page_width,
          "px"
        ),
        
        # Fixed height
        height = "800px"
      )
    )
  })
  
  
  output$page2_container <- renderUI({
    
    df <- plot_data()
    
    number_of_x_points <- n_distinct(
      df$XLabel,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
    
    individual_panel_width <- max(
      320,
      140 + (number_of_x_points * 35)
    )
    
    # Page 2 also has four graph columns
    complete_page_width <- individual_panel_width * 4
    
    tags$div(
      style = paste0(
        "width: 100%;",
        "overflow-x: auto;",
        "overflow-y: hidden;",
        "display: block;"
      ),
      
      plotOutput(
        outputId = "page2",
        
        # Dynamic width
        width = paste0(
          complete_page_width,
          "px"
        ),
        
        # Fixed height
        height = "1200px"
      )
    )
  })
  
  output$page1 <- renderPlot({
    make_page1(plot_data(), species())
  }, res = 120)
  
  output$page2 <- renderPlot({
    make_page2(plot_data(), species())
  }, res = 120)
  
  output$preview <- renderTable({
    plot_data()
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
